subject: Chemistry
title: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
summary: Atoms bond to become more stable (lower energy). Ionic bonds form by electron transfer (Na⁺Cl⁻), covalent bonds by sharing (H₂, CH₄). The Kossel–Lewis octet rule is a good start, but it has exceptions (BF₃, PCl₅, NO).

Bond parameters — bond length, bond angle, bond enthalpy and bond order — are linked: higher bond order means shorter length and higher bond enthalpy. Resonance and dipole moment describe the true structure and polarity of molecules.

VSEPR theory predicts shape from repulsion between electron pairs (lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp). Valence bond theory explains shapes and bond angles through orbital overlap and hybridisation (sp, sp², sp³, sp³d, sp³d²).

Molecular orbital theory correctly gives bond order and magnetic behaviour — O₂ is paramagnetic, which a Lewis structure cannot explain. Hydrogen bonding explains boiling points, solubility and why ice floats.

formulas.name: Octet rule and exceptions
formulas.formula: Atoms reach 8 valence electrons;  incomplete octet: BeCl₂ (4), BF₃ (6);  odd electron: NO, NO₂;  expanded octet (3rd period onwards): PCl₅ (10), SF₆ (12)
formulas.mistake: 2nd-period elements (C, N, O, F) never expand their octet — they have no d orbitals.

formulas.name: Formal charge
formulas.formula: FC = V − L − ½B   (V = valence e⁻, L = lone-pair e⁻, B = bonding e⁻)
formulas.note: The structure with the smallest formal charges is the most stable.

formulas.name: Ionic bond favourable when
formulas.formula: low ionisation enthalpy (metal) + high electron gain enthalpy (non-metal) + high lattice enthalpy
formulas.when: Whether an ionic bond will form.
formulas.note: Lattice enthalpy is higher for small, highly charged ions (MgO > NaCl).

formulas.name: Fajans' rules
formulas.formula: Covalent character increases when the cation is small, the cation's charge is high, the anion is large, or the cation has a pseudo-noble-gas (18e⁻) configuration
formulas.note: LiCl is more covalent than NaCl; AlCl₃ is largely covalent.

formulas.name: Bond order and its effects
formulas.formula: BO ↑ ⇒ bond length ↓, bond enthalpy ↑, stability ↑;  C–C 154 pm > C=C 134 pm > C≡C 120 pm

formulas.name: Resonance
formulas.formula: The real structure is a hybrid of all canonical forms;  O₃, CO₃²⁻ (BO 4/3), NO₃⁻, C₆H₆;  the resonance hybrid is more stable than any canonical form

formulas.name: Dipole moment
formulas.formula: μ = q × d;  unit debye (1 D = 3.336 × 10⁻³⁰ C·m);  vector sum of bond dipoles
formulas.note: Symmetric molecules (CO₂, BF₃, CH₄, CCl₄) have net μ = 0 even with polar bonds.

formulas.name: Percentage ionic character
formulas.formula: % ionic = (μ_observed / μ_ionic) × 100;   μ_ionic = e × d (4.8 D per Å)

formulas.name: VSEPR repulsion order
formulas.note: CH₄ 109.5° > NH₃ 107° > H₂O 104.5° — more lone pairs, smaller angle.

formulas.name: VSEPR shapes
formulas.formula: 2 bp: linear;  3 bp: trigonal planar;  2 bp + 1 lp: bent (SO₂);  4 bp: tetrahedral;  3 bp + 1 lp: pyramidal (NH₃);  2 bp + 2 lp: bent (H₂O);  5 bp: trigonal bipyramidal (PCl₅);  4 bp + 1 lp: see-saw (SF₄);  3 bp + 2 lp: T-shape (ClF₃);  2 bp + 3 lp: linear (XeF₂, I₃⁻);  6 bp: octahedral (SF₆);  5 bp + 1 lp: square pyramidal (BrF₅);  4 bp + 2 lp: square planar (XeF₄)

formulas.name: Hybridisation shortcut
formulas.formula: H = ½(V + M − c + a)   (V = valence e⁻ of central atom, M = monovalent atoms, c = cation charge, a = anion charge);  2 sp, 3 sp², 4 sp³, 5 sp³d, 6 sp³d², 7 sp³d³
formulas.mistake: Divalent atoms like O and S are not counted in M.

formulas.name: Hybrid orbitals and angles
formulas.formula: sp 180° (BeCl₂, C₂H₂);  sp² 120° (BF₃, C₂H₄);  sp³ 109.5° (CH₄);  sp³d 90°, 120° (PCl₅);  sp³d² 90° (SF₆)
formulas.note: In PCl₅ the axial bonds are longer than the equatorial ones (more repulsion).

formulas.name: Sigma and pi bonds
formulas.formula: Every single bond = 1σ;  double = 1σ + 1π;  triple = 1σ + 2π;  σ by head-on overlap (strong), π by sideways overlap (weak)
formulas.mistake: π bonds are not formed by hybrid orbitals; an s orbital cannot form a π bond.

formulas.name: MOT bond order and magnetism
formulas.formula: BO = ½(N_b − N_a);  BO > 0 ⇒ molecule can exist;  unpaired e⁻ ⇒ paramagnetic

formulas.name: MO energy order
formulas.formula: Up to N₂ (14 e⁻): σ1s < σ*1s < σ2s < σ*2s < (π2pₓ = π2p_y) < σ2p_z < (π*2pₓ = π*2p_y) < σ*2p_z;   for O₂, F₂: σ2p_z lies below π2p
formulas.note: B₂ and O₂ are paramagnetic; N₂, F₂, C₂ are diamagnetic.

formulas.name: Hydrogen bonding
formulas.formula: H bonded to F, O or N is attracted to a lone pair on another F/O/N;  intermolecular (H₂O, HF — high bp) and intramolecular (o-nitrophenol — low bp, volatile)
formulas.mistake: Intramolecular H-bonding does not raise the boiling point; it lowers it (no association).

examples.title: Formal charge in O₃
examples.problem: Formal charge on the central O of O₃? (2 bonds — one double, one single — and 1 lone pair)
examples.solution: FC = 6 − 2 − ½ × 6 = +1. The singly bonded O has −1, the doubly bonded O has 0.

examples.title: Bond orders of the O₂ family
examples.problem: Bond orders and stability order of O₂, O₂⁺, O₂⁻, O₂²⁻?
examples.solution: O₂ = 2, O₂⁺ = 2.5, O₂⁻ = 1.5, O₂²⁻ = 1. Stability and bond enthalpy: O₂⁺ > O₂ > O₂⁻ > O₂²⁻; bond length the reverse.

examples.title: Hybridisation shortcut
examples.problem: Hybridisation and shape of SF₄, XeF₄, NH₄⁺?
examples.solution: SF₄: ½(6 + 4) = 5 ⇒ sp³d, see-saw (1 lp). XeF₄: ½(8 + 4) = 6 ⇒ sp³d², square planar (2 lp). NH₄⁺: ½(5 + 4 − 1) = 4 ⇒ sp³, tetrahedral.

examples.title: % ionic character of HCl
examples.problem: HCl: μ = 1.03 D, bond length 1.27 Å. % ionic?

examples.title: Counting σ and π
examples.problem: σ and π bonds in CH₂=CH–C≡N (acrylonitrile)?
examples.solution: σ: 3 C–H + 1 of C=C + 1 C–C + 1 of C≡N = 6. π: 1 in C=C + 2 in C≡N = 3.

examples.title: Dipole of NH₃ vs NF₃
examples.problem: Why is the dipole moment of NH₃ (1.47 D) larger than that of NF₃ (0.23 D)?
examples.solution: In NH₃ the N–H bond dipoles and the lone-pair dipole point the same way (they add); in NF₃ the N–F bond dipoles point opposite to the lone pair (they cancel).

examples.title: Magnetism of N₂ and O₂
examples.problem: Which of N₂ and O₂ is paramagnetic, and why?
examples.solution: N₂: BO = 3, all electrons paired ⇒ diamagnetic. O₂: 2 unpaired electrons in π*2p ⇒ paramagnetic (a Lewis structure can't show this).

topics.title: Kossel–Lewis approach
topics.explain: Noble gases are stable because their octet is complete. Other atoms complete their octet by giving/taking electrons (ionic) or sharing them (covalent). Lewis dot structures show valence electrons as dots.

topics.title: Ionic bond and lattice enthalpy
topics.explain: Lattice enthalpy is the energy needed to break one mole of an ionic solid into gaseous ions. Higher lattice enthalpy = more stable solid, higher melting point. It is found with the Born–Haber cycle.

topics.title: Bond parameters
topics.explain: Bond length: distance between nuclei (grows with atomic size). Bond angle: angle between bonds at the central atom. Bond enthalpy: energy to break one mole of bonds. Bond order: number of bonds between two atoms.

topics.title: Valence bond theory
topics.explain: A bond forms when two half-filled orbitals overlap and their electrons pair up. Greater overlap = stronger bond. Overlaps: s–s, s–p, p–p head-on (σ), sideways p–p (π).

topics.title: Rules of hybridisation
topics.explain: Orbitals of nearly equal energy on the same atom mix; the number of hybrid orbitals equals the number mixed; hybrid orbitals hold only σ bonds and lone pairs. Ethane sp³, ethene sp², ethyne sp.

topics.title: Basics of MOT
topics.explain: Atomic orbitals combine into bonding (lower energy) and antibonding (higher energy) MOs. LCAO: only orbitals of matching symmetry and similar energy combine. He₂ has BO 0 — it doesn't exist. H₂⁺ and He₂⁺ have BO 0.5.

topics.title: Electronegativity and metallic bonding
topics.explain: Electronegativity is an atom's tendency to pull shared electrons towards itself (F highest, 4.0). A large electronegativity difference (above ~1.7) ⇒ mostly ionic bond; small ⇒ polar covalent; zero ⇒ non-polar. Metallic bonding: a 'sea' of delocalised electrons among positive metal ions — which is why metals conduct and are malleable and ductile.

topics.title: Effects of hydrogen bonding
topics.explain: HF, H₂O and NH₃ have higher boiling points than the other hydrides of their groups. Ice has an open cage structure ⇒ it is lighter than water. Alcohols and carboxylic acids dissolve in water. Protein and DNA structures depend on H-bonds.

ratta: Fajans: small cation, high charge, large anion ⇒ more covalent.
lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp;  CH₄ 109.5° > NH₃ 107° > H₂O 104.5°.
H = ½(V + M − c + a): 2 sp, 3 sp², 4 sp³, 5 sp³d, 6 sp³d².
SF₄ see-saw, ClF₃ T-shape, XeF₂ linear, XeF₄ square planar, BrF₅ square pyramidal.
BO = ½(N_b − N_a);  O₂ & B₂ paramagnetic.
μ = 0: CO₂, BF₃, CH₄, CCl₄;  NH₃ > NF₃.
